inline_text: ### Project Name Observal ### Project Description Observal is an open-source (Apache-2.0), self-hosted registry and system of record for the agentic resources organizations build for their coding agents: Agent Skills, MCP servers, hooks, prompts, sandboxes, and the agents that bundle them. It also includes an insight engine that shows which agentic resources are actually used and whether they help. **Scope.** Observal works with the MCP *clients* that coding agents run in (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, Goose, and so on). It is not an MCP server registry or a public MCP directory. It governs what gets installed into those clients, renders each client's native configuration, and measures what happens afterwards, so it does not overlap with MCP server registries. **Where does Observal fit in your modern enterprise infrastructure?** **Problem.** Every engineering organization now produces internal skills, MCP servers, and agent configurations. They end up in siloed repositories, are rewritten for each harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, Copilot, Goose, and others), and are rebuilt by teams who don't know they already exist. Authors can't see how their agentic resources are used, and agent failures rarely produce error codes, so the feedback loop never closes. **What Observal does** - **Registry.** Versioned, reviewed publishing of agents and five agentic resource types, with team namespaces, visibility controls, and a pull-request-style review workflow. - **Write once, install anywhere.** An agent is defined once and Observal generates native configuration for 10 harnesses (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Kiro, Copilot in VS Code, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Antigravity, Goose, Pi), tracked by a lockfile. - **Discovery and delegation on open standards.** Approved resources are published as Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD v0.91) entries with `urn:air:` identifiers at `/.well-known/ard.json`. Agents delegate to other approved agents, local or remote, as A2A v1.0 Tasks through a bundled MCP server, with bounded depth, fan-out, and loop protection. - **Traces.** Hooks capture each session as a structured trace (prompts, tool calls, MCP round trips, tokens, errors), attributed to the exact agent and agentic resource versions installed. - **Insights.** Reports built from session evidence (via LiteLLM, any provider) on what works, what gets in the way, and suggested fixes, linked to the supporting traces. - **Fully self-hosted.** Postgres, ClickHouse, and Redis on the operator's infrastructure (Docker Compose, Kubernetes/Terraform). No data leaves the operator. SSO, SCIM, audit logs, and dashboards are all in the Apache-2.0 distribution; there is no closed enterprise edition. **History.** Public repository created 2026-03-30; first release 2026-04-21; 46 releases, latest v1.15.0 (2026-10-14); about 2,550 commits. We started it after seeing that teams build agentic resources (skills, MCP servers, agent configs) that then get abandoned: nobody can find them, and users rarely report when one doesn't work, so authors never get the feedback to fix them. ### Alignment with AAIF Mission AAIF exists "to drive adoption and growth of open source agentic AI in the broader community." Observal addresses the adoption problem inside organizations: companies have adopted agents but can't share, govern, or measure the agentic resources they build for them. - **Vendor neutrality.** One agent definition runs on 10 harnesses from competing vendors, preventing per-vendor lock-in of an organization's agentic resources. - **Open standards first.** Discovery uses ARD, delegation uses A2A, tool connectivity uses MCP, and skill packaging is moving to full Agent Skills conformance. Observal avoids proprietary formats where an open one exists. - **Trust and governance.** Review workflows, provenance, version-pinned attribution, and audit logs, in line with the "Observability & Traceability" and "Governance, Risk & Regulatory Alignment" working groups. - **Neutral stewardship.** Organizations will make an internal registry their system of record only if no single vendor controls it. Foundation governance is the credible way to provide that. ### Relation to Existing AAIF Projects **Hosted projects** - **MCP:** registers, versions, reviews, and distributes MCP servers; captures MCP round trips in traces; ships its own MCP server for delegation. - **A2A:** native A2A v1.0 client. Remote agents are registered by Agent Card URL, reviewed, and pinned by digest; Observal never proxies their traffic. - **Goose:** supported harness (Goose 1.10+, verified on 1.45.0) via a Goose hook plugin. - **AGENTS.md:** Observal manages AGENTS.md files as a resource type. For the Pi harness, AGENTS.md is the agent file: installing an agent writes its AGENTS.md. - **Agentgateway and Agent Router:** complementary, with no overlap in function. See "Why Observal does not overlap with Agentgateway or Agent Router" below. **TC-approved project (paperwork in progress)** - **Agent Skills (#47):** first-class resource type; ROADMAP.md commits to full spec conformance, including vendoring the official `skills-ref` validator. **Why Observal does not overlap with Agentgateway or Agent Router** Both are runtime components that sit in the request path. Observal never does. It acts at install time and after the session, and its data comes from the client, not from proxied traffic. | | Agentgateway / Agent Router | Observal | | --- | --- | --- | | Where it sits | In the network path between agents, tools, and models | Beside the path: a registry plus hooks inside the coding-agent client | | When it acts | At request time: routing, policy, auth, rate limits | Before a session (publish, review, install) and after it (traces, insights) | | Unit it manages | Live traffic and connections | Versioned agents and agentic resources (skills, MCP servers, hooks, prompts, sandboxes) | | Output | Routed, authorized, or blocked requests | Native config for 10 clients, a lockfile, version-attributed traces, insight reports | | Observability source | Proxied traffic | Client hooks (prompts, tool calls, tokens, errors), tied to installed versions | What Observal does not do: - It does not proxy, route, or load-balance MCP, A2A, or model traffic. Remote A2A agents are called directly with the reviewed Agent Card; Observal never proxies their traffic or stores their credentials. - It does not enforce runtime auth or traffic policy. Its policy is review and approval before something can be installed. - It does not replace a gateway's observability. A gateway sees what crossed the wire; Observal sees what the agent session did and which agentic resource versions were installed. They can be deployed together. **Adjacent proposals under review.** Observal is not a public MCP directory, a traffic gateway, a runtime policy engine, or a packaging or wire-format standard, so it sits next to rather than on top of MCP Gateway Registry (#29), ContextForge (#39), Prismor (#51), Weft (#53), Agent Plugins (#56) and AGNTCY (#57). The differences: Observal versions multi-component agents, compiles harness-native configuration across 10 clients, and closes the loop with attributed session evidence. Both MCP Gateway Registry and ContextForge overlap with Observal only on the registry part, not on harness rendering or insights: - **MCP Gateway Registry (#29):** a self-hosted registry for MCP servers, A2A agents, and skills that sits in front of runtime traffic as a gateway. It shares the "internal catalog of agentic resources" story, but it does not compile configs for 10 harnesses or tie session traces to installed versions. - **ContextForge (#39):** a gateway, registry, and observability bundle, postponed because of overlap with Agentgateway and Agent Router. Its observability covers proxied traffic; Observal's comes from harness hooks and feeds insight reports. Observal has no gateway component, so it does not carry that overlap. We plan to integrate the Agent Plugins spec once it is more widely adopted and to evaluate mapping ARD entries to AGNTCY's OASF. We are glad to coordinate with each team on boundaries. ### Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption **Use cases** - A platform team publishes a reviewed code-review skill once; every team installs it in whichever harness they use. - Debugging agent failures from version-attributed traces. - Observing MCP tool calls across sessions and teams. - Sharing agent configurations through team registries. - Delegating part of a task to another team's approved agent or a remote A2A service. **Named adopters outside Observal Inc.** (production vs. evaluation stated for each) - Appian Corporation: maintains a public fork, https://github.com/appian/Observal (created 2026-09-30). Hemalatha Madeswaran, an Observal maintainer, works at Appian. Appian runs Observal in production as its internal registry for agentic resources. **Ecosystem integrations** (acknowledged by the other project; not adopters) - ARD reference implementations: pull request adding Observal, open, https://github.com/ards-project/ard-docs/pull/25 **Project signals (as of 2026-10-13)** - 4,265 GitHub stars, 1,130 forks, 65 contributors, 45 releases - About 1,940 Discord members - `observal-cli` on PyPI: about 500 downloads per month - OpenSSF Best Practices Gold (100%), project 13472 - OpenSSF Scorecard 9.8 / 10 (v5.3.0, run 2026-10-13) **Disclosures on these numbers** - Observal Inc. funds a contributor-recognition budget (about $4,000/month, public ledger on [Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/observal); how it works is documented in [Contributor Payments](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/docs/contributor-payments.md), linked from CONTRIBUTING.md). About 7 of the 65 contributors have received payments through this budget. - The fork count reflects strong community interest and people wanting to contribute. ### Technical Committee Sponsor (if identified) _No response_ ### GitHub Repository URL https://github.com/Observal/Observal ### License Apache 2.0 ### Governance Model [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md) defines a merit-based model with three roles (Contributor, Core Contributor, Maintainer): nomination with evidence, Maintainer promotion by a majority of active Maintainers, routine vs. broad decisions, conflict resolution, a 6-month inactivity/Emeritus process, and governance changes by public PR. On acceptance the project will adopt the Linux Foundation (LF) technical charter and replace its CLA with the LF IP policy (DCO). ### CI/CD & Release Workflow GitHub Actions workflows: ci, e2e-frontend, codeql, dependency-review, gitleaks, scorecard, sbom, release, deploy, and terraform, plus Renovate and Codecov integrations. Development happens on `main`. Since v1.14, releases are published only from protected `release/X.Y` branches ([docs/self-hosting/releasing.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/docs/self-hosting/releasing.md)): - Each minor line has one release branch that carries alpha, beta, release candidates, stable, and patches. There is no `develop` branch. - Fixes land on `main` first and are cherry-picked with provenance into each affected release line. Release branches are never merged into `main`, rebased, or force-pushed. - A release PR against `release/X.Y` updates versions, release notes, and the changelog. Pushing it publishes from the exact validated commit. Tags are keyless-signed and tied to the release branch. - Artifacts: PyPI (`observal-cli`), npm, GHCR images, and Helm charts. Changes are recorded in CHANGELOG.md. - Cadence: 45 releases between 2026-04-21 and 2026-10-04 (latest v1.14.0). ### Public-Facing Contribution Process for Specifications Design decisions are made in public: - [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) covers issue claiming (`/take`, `/drop`), branch naming, review, and changelog rules. - Larger changes are discussed first on Discord (#contributing, #feature-requests) or GitHub Discussions, before code is written. ### Publicly Accessible Issue Tracker https://github.com/Observal/Observal/issues ### External Project Dependencies - **Server (Python), MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0:** FastAPI, Starlette, Uvicorn, SQLAlchemy, asyncpg, Pydantic, Alembic, httpx, LiteLLM, redis-py, arq, Strawberry GraphQL, Authlib, cryptography, python3-saml, PyJWT, structlog. - **CLI (Python), MIT/BSD/Apache-2.0:** Typer, Click, Rich, PyYAML, docker-py. - **Web, MIT:** React, Vite. - **Runtime services:** PostgreSQL (PostgreSQL License), ClickHouse (Apache-2.0), nginx (BSD-2-Clause), Prometheus (Apache-2.0, optional). - **Copyleft and source-available runtime services (not linked into Observal, run as separate containers):** Redis 8 (`redis:8-alpine` in the Compose stack; RSALv2, SSPLv1, or AGPLv3 at the user's option) and Grafana (AGPLv3, optional). The full list with licenses is available from the project SBOM. ### Maintainers & Contributors Active maintainers (MAINTAINERS.md): - Hari Srinivasan (@Haz3-jolt), Observal Inc. - Subramania Raja (@dhanpraja231), Observal Inc. - Shaan Narendran (@ShaanNarendran), Observal Inc. - Ryan Madhuwala (@RAWx18), Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust (DT) Lab leader - Hemalatha Madeswaran (@HemalathaMadeswaran18), Appian Corporation 65 contributors in total. About 7 have received payments through Observal Inc.'s contributor-recognition budget (see Example Use Cases and Evidence of Adoption). ### Leadership Team & Decision Process **Leadership team:** the active Maintainers ([MAINTAINERS.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md)): Hari Srinivasan (@Haz3-jolt), Subramania Raja (@dhanpraja231), Shaan Narendran (@ShaanNarendran), Ryan Madhuwala (@RAWx18), Hemalatha Madeswaran (@HemalathaMadeswaran18). **Decision process:** routine decisions are made by the Maintainer or Core Contributor who owns the affected area. Cross-cutting decisions (architecture, compatibility, security, public APIs) need open discussion with the relevant Maintainers and affected contributors before implementation. Disagreements are settled by technical discussion based on evidence, requirements, and maintainability. If consensus cannot be reached, the area Maintainer makes the final call and documents it, and project-wide decisions are made by the Maintainers together. Maintainers decide on technical merit, security, reliability, and user impact, not on personal, organizational, or commercial interests. Full text in [GOVERNANCE.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md). ### Roadmap [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) covers August 2026 to August 2027, with per-item status, priority, and "complete when" criteria, organized into three lanes: - **Observability:** cross-harness session and attribution correctness, an insights and dashboard feedback loop, component insights, and success-criteria evaluation. - **Agentic resources lifecycle:** Agent Skills specification alignment (including a vendored reference validator), configurable pull-request-style review, and Git webhook version sync. - **Platform:** CLI and skills, teamspaces, hosting paths, administration, CI/CD, and project security controls. ### Security - OpenSSF Best Practices Gold (100%): https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/13472 - OpenSSF Scorecard 9.8 / 10 (v5.3.0, run 2026-10-13): https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/Observal/Observal - [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/SECURITY.md): private vulnerability reporting through GitHub Security Advisories or email, with a 48-hour acknowledgement target. - Automated checks: CodeQL, gitleaks, dependency review, SBOM, property-based fuzz tests (Hypothesis), & Renovate dependency updates. - Self-hosted by design: telemetry stays on operator infrastructure, and database ports bind to loopback by default. ### Website URL https://observal.io/ ### Documented Governance Practices (if any) - [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/SECURITY.md) - [AI_POLICY.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/AI_POLICY.md) - [CLA.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/CLA.md) - [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) ### Links to Social Media Accounts Discord: https://discord.observal.io, LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/observal-io/, YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@Observal-io, GitHub Discussions: https://github.com/Observal/Observal/discussions ### Trademark and accounts - [x] If the project is accepted, I agree to donate all project trademarks and accounts to the AAIF. ### Details of Existing Financial Sponsorship Observal Inc. (Delaware C-corp) is the sole sponsor. It funds engineering time and a fixed contributor-recognition budget of about $4,000 USD per month. The budget is tracked publicly on the [Observal Open Collective](https://opencollective.com/observal), where Observal Inc. is its own fiscal host, and is described in [Contributor Payments](https://github.com/Observal/Observal/blob/main/docs/contributor-payments.md). Payments are recognition for sustained contributions, not salary or a retainer. No other sponsors or grants. ### Infrastructure Needs or Requests - CI minutes for end-to-end and multi-harness tests (10 harnesses). - A hosted public demo instance. - A third-party security audit. ### Additional Information **Requested stage: Sandbox.** **Sandbox thesis.** Organizations need an open, vendor-neutral system of record for the agentic resources they build internally, built on MCP, A2A, Agent Skills, and ARD rather than on any one harness vendor's format. Observal is a working implementation of that, with more than six months of public history. **What would justify moving to Growth** 1. Adoption by many more organizations, with three or more named independent production adopters. 2. Maintainers from at least three organizations other than Observal Inc. (today two: LF Decentralized Trust Lab and Appian), with sustained merge activity from each. 3. Full Agent Skills conformance, plus upstream contributions to ARD and A2A. 4. A documented, versioned trace and attribution schema that other tools can produce and consume. ### Application contact name(s) and email(s) Hari Srinivasan hari@observal.io, Subramania Raja subramania.raja@observal.io ### Contributing or sponsoring entity signatory information | Name | Address | Type (e.g., Delaware corporation) | Signatory name and title | Email address | |-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-----------| | Observal Inc. | 8 The Green, Suite A, Dover, DE 19901, USA | Delaware corporation | Hari Srinivasan, CTO | hari@observal.io |
